target: Umarım yakında iyileşirsin.
english: I hope you recover soon.
tip: Umarım, I hope, is followed by the aorist here: iyileşirsin (iyileş + ir + sin) = you get better.

target: Başarısızlığa rağmen pes etmedi.
english: He didn't give up despite failure.
tip: rağmen, despite, needs the noun in dative: Başarısızlığa rağmen (başarısızlık + a) = despite failure.

target: Hadi bakalım, işe başlayalım.
english: Alright then, let's get to work.
tip: -alım means let's: başlayalım (başla + yalım) = let's start, the we-form suggestion ending.

target: Bana göre bu fikir çok mantıklı.
english: In my opinion this idea is very logical.
tip: göre takes the dative and means according to: Bana göre = in my opinion, bana being the dative of ben.

target: Duvardaki saat durmuş, pili bitmiş olmalı.
english: The clock on the wall has stopped; the battery must be dead.
tip: -mış olmalı means must have or probably has: bitmiş olmalı = the battery must have died, a guess from evidence.

target: Ağaçların gölgesinde oturup dinlenmek çok güzel.
english: It is very nice to sit and rest in the shade of trees.
tip: -ip links verbs sharing one subject; only the last carries tense: oturup dinlenmek = to sit and rest.

target: Yıllardır burada yaşıyorum ama hâlâ keşfedecek yerler var.
english: I've been living here for years but there are still places to discover.
tip: For an action still going, put -dır on the time span plus present tense: Yıllardır ... yaşıyorum = I have lived here for years.

target: Oyuncu sahnede harika oynadı, seyirciler ayakta alkışlamış.
english: The actor performed wonderfully on stage; apparently the audience gave a standing ovation.
tip: -di is what you saw, -miş what you only heard: oynadı = performed (seen), alkışlamış = apparently applauded (reported).

target: İşe yürüyerek gidiyorum, yakın.
english: I walk to work, it's close.
tip: yürüyerek means by walking. Add -erek or -arak to a verb stem to say how an action is done: yürü plus -yerek.

target: Eve döndüğümde çok yorgundum.
english: When I returned home I was very tired.
tip: döndüğümde means when I returned. The -düğümde ending turns a verb into a when I did X time clause.

target: Erken kalksaydım otobüsü kaçırmazdım.
english: If I had gotten up early I wouldn't have missed the bus.
tip: kalksaydım means if I had gotten up. The -saydım ending marks a past condition that did not actually happen.

target: Mavi gömlek kırmızıdan daha ucuz.
english: The blue shirt is cheaper than the red one.
tip: kırmızıdan daha ucuz means cheaper than the red. Mark the compared thing with -dan and add daha before the adjective.

target: Param olsa dünyayı gezmek isterdim.
english: If I had money I would want to travel the world.
tip: olsa means if I had. Plain -sa, not -saydı, states a present unreal wish, paired with isterdim, I would want.

target: Kuzenlerimle her yaz denize giderdik.
english: We used to go to the sea with my cousins every summer.
tip: giderdik means we used to go. The -erdik ending describes a repeated habit in the past, not a single event.

target: Eğer yardıma ihtiyacın olursa beni ara.
english: If you need help call me.
tip: Eğer means if, but it is optional. The -sa on olursa already carries the condition, so Eğer just reinforces it.

target: Her gün metroya binip işe giderim.
english: I take the metro to work every day.
tip: binip means get on and. The -ip ending links two verbs sharing one subject; only the last, giderim, takes the tense.

target: Para biriktirirsem gelecek yıl tatile gideceğim.
english: If I save money I'll go on vacation next year.
tip: biriktirirsem means if I save. The -sem here sets a real future condition, so the main verb is future, gideceğim.

target: Küçük kızım okula yeni başladı, çok heyecanlı.
english: My little daughter just started school, very excited.
tip: okula başladı means started school. başlamak takes the dative, so it attaches -a to okul, literally started to school.

target: Bu kitabı yazan yazar çok ünlü birisi.
english: The author who wrote this book is a very famous person.
tip: yazan means who wrote. Add -an or -en to a verb when the noun after it did the action: yaz plus -an describes yazar.

target: Annemin yaptığı börek her zaman çok lezzetli olur.
english: The pastry my mother makes is always very delicious.
tip: yaptığı means that she makes. Use -tığı, not -an, when someone else is the doer: annem makes the börek.

target: Evde mi yemek istersin yoksa dışarı mı çıkalım?
english: Would you rather eat at home or go out?
tip: mi marks what is being asked about. Placed after Evde and dışarı, with yoksa between, it offers an either-or choice.

target: Yağmura rağmen dışarı çıktık.
english: We went out despite the rain.
tip: rağmen means despite. The noun before it takes the dative, so it is Yağmura, not Yağmur.

target: Haberlere göre yarın kar yağacakmış.
english: According to the news, it will apparently snow tomorrow.
tip: yağacakmış means it will apparently snow. Adding -mış to the future -acak marks news you heard, not witnessed.

target: Haberlere göre deprem çok şiddetli olmuş.
english: According to the news, the earthquake was very strong.
tip: Haberlere göre means according to the news. göre takes the dative, so it is Haberler plus -e.

target: Fiyat uygun olursa bu evi alalım.
english: If the price is reasonable let's buy this house.
tip: alalım means let's buy. The -alım ending on a verb makes a first-person plural suggestion, let's do it.

target: Babam gençken çok sportif bir insanmış.
english: My father was apparently a very athletic person when young.
tip: gençken means when he was young. Attach -ken to a word to mean while or when that state held.

target: Düğün bir Haziran'da.
english: The wedding is in June.
tip: Month names and proper nouns take an apostrophe before a suffix: Haziran'da (Haziran + da = in June).

target: Toplantı iki buçukta başlıyor.
english: The meeting starts at half past two.
tip: For half past, say the hour then buçuk: iki buçukta = at two and a half, meaning half past two.

target: Artık soğuk havaya alıştı.
english: He is used to the cold weather now.
tip: The verb alışmak takes the dative: havaya alıştı = got used to the weather, hava plus ya.

target: Meğer yanlış adrese gitmişiz.
english: It turns out we went to the wrong address.
tip: Meğer flags a fact you just realized and pairs with the -miş past: gitmişiz = turns out we went.
